title: Aft Engine Mount Shear Tie — Removal

issue.reason: Original issue of the aft engine mount shear tie removal task.

abstract: Removal of the one-piece aft engine mount shear tie from the pylon rib, including the fairing structure that has to be opened before the tie can be withdrawn outboard past the rib.

sections.purpose: This task gives the removal of the aft engine mount shear tie from the pylon, including the opening of the pylon fairing structure that the withdrawal path needs.
sections.job_setup_note: The engine must be removed or supported on the engine change trolley with the load taken off the aft mount. The fan cowl doors must be open and held on their stays. The tie cannot be withdrawn past the pylon lower access panel, so the lower fairing panels and the aft fairing closing rib have to come off first; allow for that in the job planning, because it is the larger part of the elapsed time and it needs the fairing sealant to be renewed at build-up.
sections.procedure: 1. WARNING: DO NOT SLACKEN ANY AFT MOUNT FASTENER UNTIL THE ENGINE LOAD IS TAKEN BY THE TROLLEY OR THE ENGINE IS REMOVED. 2. Open the fan cowl doors and put them on their stays. 3. Remove the pylon lower access panel. 4. Remove the pylon lower fairing panels and the aft fairing closing rib and put them on the padded trestle; the shear tie cannot pass the access panel aperture and this is the only withdrawal path. 5. Disconnect the harness support from the inboard face and move it clear. 6. Check the clearance to the mount microswitch 152PP and to the position actuator 498PP5 and protect both against damage. 7. CAUTION: DO NOT USE THE MOUNT FITTING AS A STEP OR AS A TOOL REST. A LOCAL DENT IS A REJECTABLE CONDITION. 8. Slacken the fasteners in the release sequence given on the joint diagram, one turn at a time across the joint. 9. Withdraw the shear tie D5450123089978 outboard past the pylon rib and through the fairing aperture. 10. Recover the washers AES161398-12 and count them against the joint diagram. 11. Examine the pylon rib land for fretting, for corrosion and for hole elongation. 12. Bag and identify the removed items.
sections.close_out: Protect the open joint, the exposed rib land and the open fairing aperture against damage and moisture. Make sure that every fastener and washer is accounted for against the joint diagram. Record the rib land condition in the aircraft technical record.

safety_precautions: Take the engine load on the trolley before any mount fastener is slackened.
Put the fan cowl doors on their stays.
Put the warning notices in the flight compartment.

title: Aft Engine Mount Shear Tie — Removal

issue.reason: Task split by embodiment standard: the fairing opening sequence kept for the one-piece fleet and a direct withdrawal sequence added for the two-piece standard.

abstract: Removal of the aft engine mount shear tie from the pylon rib, split by embodiment standard: the two-piece halves come out through the access panel while the one-piece item still needs the pylon fairing opened.

sections.purpose: This task gives the removal of the aft engine mount shear tie from the pylon, in the one-piece or the two-piece standard as fitted to the aircraft.
sections.job_setup_note: The engine must be removed or supported on the engine change trolley with the load taken off the aft mount. The fan cowl doors must be open and held on their stays. The load path release sequence and the withdrawal path both differ between the two standards and the applicable one must be identified from the aircraft technical record before any fastener is slackened. On the one-piece standard the pylon lower fairing panels and the aft fairing closing rib still have to come off, because the tie will not pass the access panel aperture; on the two-piece standard the halves come out through the access panel and the fairing stays closed, which is where the whole saving of the change sits.
sections.procedure: 1. WARNING: DO NOT SLACKEN ANY AFT MOUNT FASTENER UNTIL THE ENGINE LOAD IS TAKEN BY THE TROLLEY OR THE ENGINE IS REMOVED. 2. Open the fan cowl doors and put them on their stays. 3. Remove the pylon lower access panel. 4. On the one-piece standard only, remove the pylon lower fairing panels and the aft fairing closing rib and put them on the padded trestle. Do not remove them on the two-piece standard. 5. Disconnect the harness support from the inboard face and move it clear. 6. Check the clearance to the mount microswitch 152PP and to the position actuator 498PP5 and protect both against damage. 7. CAUTION: DO NOT USE THE MOUNT FITTING AS A STEP OR AS A TOOL REST. A LOCAL DENT IS A REJECTABLE CONDITION. 8. Slacken the fasteners in the release sequence given for the fitted standard, one turn at a time across the joint. 9. On the two-piece standard, remove the splice plate D5450121271272 first and then each half of the shear tie through the access panel aperture. 10. On the one-piece standard, withdraw the shear tie D5450123089978 outboard past the pylon rib and through the fairing aperture. 11. Recover the washers AES161398-12 and count them against the joint diagram. 12. Examine the pylon rib land for fretting, for corrosion and for hole elongation. 13. Bag and identify the removed items.
sections.close_out: Protect the open joint and the exposed rib land against damage and moisture. Make sure that every fastener and washer is accounted for against the joint diagram. Record the rib land condition and the fitted standard in the aircraft technical record.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. Identify the fitted shear tie standard from the aircraft technical record before the release sequence and the withdrawal path are selected. Manhours are given for the two-piece standard; add six hours for the fairing removal and build-up on the one-piece standard.

safety_precautions: Take the engine load on the trolley before any mount fastener is slackened.
Put the fan cowl doors on their stays.
Put the warning notices in the flight compartment.
